# T0.17 — the repetition loop inside the benchmark's function, as TSVC has it (packaging v6): does a temporary array cost once again, and does anything else change?

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** done

## The question

The author, 4 Oct, on the clean layout (v5): "I do not like that this solution make the speed up worse … the tmp array is also a problem". In v5 the function is ONE repetition, called 48 times, so a temporary array obtained inside it is obtained on every call. Layout tested (v6, suite `tsvc_c2`): v5 with the repetition loop and TSVC's `dummy` call inside the function, where TSVC's own function has them. Per loop: identical output; the expert reference as fast as in the one-file packaging (v4) on the same lane, the reference with malloc/free inside the function included; DiscoPoP's view and the order statement as in v4; then sizes, classes and references through the harness.

## Result in one paragraph

Pre-flight (server and Mac, no model): the program is the same (output byte for byte, 44 of 44). Measured alike — one 12-core lane, variants interleaved — the expert references reach the same in the one-file packaging, in v5 and in v6 (median 3.27×, 3.19×, 3.32×); the 'lower ceiling' reported for v5 compared a lane with a whole node. The real cost of v5 is the temporary array: the five references that need one, written with malloc and free in the function, reach 0.39–1.09× in v5 and 1.36–2.60× in v6 (v4: 1.41–2.39×). DiscoPoP's view as in v4: server, two draws, 41 of 42 loops the same on every criterion in each, and no loop differs in both (s482 in one, s1213 in the other: which blocker the detector names). The order statement under prompt version 4 right on 168 of 168 server profiles, the repetition loop's request included. Classes on v6, three draws: R 29, A 10, D 5 — E1's 25 loops as in v4 and v5 (R 18, A 3, D 4); k17 and k42 (one repetition) become A by a pragma on the one-iteration repetition loop. All 28 references accepted through the harness (26 FASTER; class R 1.33–5.51×, median 2.95×). Adopted by the author, 5 Oct.

Without the measured fact a careful model pays for safety with all the speed; a less careful one loses the safety. **How fast the agent's successes are — new in this read-out.** Median speedup of the successes with evidence at one attempt: `k19` 1.45×, `k23` 1.40×, `k27` 1.93×, `k31` 1.37× — the expert versions through the same verification (`t0_14_c2_refs`) reach 4.14×, 3.33×, 4.17×, 3.09×; on `k48` the agent reaches 3.80× of the expert's 4.13×. Cause, read from the programs and logs: after the right split DiscoPoP reports Do-All for the loop of the assignment and not for the loop of `u[…] += …`, which reads what the loop before it wrote; the agent's directive therefore stands on one of two loops (two of three on `k27`). On `k48` the same statement's loop, reading elements nothing writes, gets its directive. Why DiscoPoP reports no pattern there is NOT examined yet — open, and the next thing to look at (a DiscoPoP defect would be fixed at the root, B-numbered). One trial without evidence found a better program than the split: in the third region it tried, after one rewrite the gate rejected (the output differed), the model shifted the first statement by one iteration and made the whole loop one parallel loop, 5.04× (`k19` rep 9, 10 calls; DiscoPoP's blockers had gone back to the model in an earlier region's conversation of that trial, not in this one). **The repetition loop:** kept as it is by every changed program of the agent (172 of 172); 2 of Opus's and 6 of Fable's programs write it two to four times — the original loop again as the fallback when an allocation fails, each copy with its `dummy` call; none removes or reorders a repetition. **Cost, API-equivalent:** 1,181 model calls, $243 — the one-attempt arms $16 and $18, the three-attempt arms $47 and $112, Haiku alone $6, Sonnet $12, Opus $7, Fable $25. Stated with it: the effect is the split's ORDER, not its full parallelization (about a third to a half of the expert's speed); feedback is a second, weaker and far costlier route to the same fact; and more attempts are not free — in this experiment they produced the agent's only unsafe programs and its only pointless ones. | 2026-10-04 | plan | **T0.17 — the repetition loop back INSIDE the benchmark's function, as TSVC has it (packaging v6, suite `tsvc_c2`): a pre-flight, no model — registered before any of it runs through the harness; no model reads these files before the author has seen them and said so.** Why: the cost the author does not accept (row below) is the LAYOUT's. Packaging v5 made the function ONE repetition and let `main.c` call it 48 times, so whatever a solution obtains inside the function it obtains on every call. TSVC's own function holds its repetition loop and calls `dummy(a, b, c, d, e, aa, bb, cc, 0.)` between two repetitions (`benchmarks/TSVC_2/src/tsvc.c`; `dummy.c`: "called in each loop to make all computations appear required"), and so did E1-final's packages — where every arm that used a temporary array obtained it in front of the loop (the counts in the row below). v5 took the loop out because v4's version of it came with a note, with `pb_mix` and with protected lines; none of those is needed to have the loop. **The form (v6):** `<name>.c` — one `#include "data.h"` and the function: `for (int nl = 0; nl < iterations; nl++) {` TSVC's loop text `dummy(a, b, c, d, e); }` — no comment, no `pb_` name, the one editable file; `data.h` — v5's plus `#define iterations N` and the prototype of `dummy`; `main.c`, ours — `dummy` (the change of a few input values that `pb_mix` made, on its own arguments, counted by its own calls) and `main` with ONE call of the function between the timer's two calls; the measurement header outside the package as in v5. No note, no protected line: what keeps the repetitions honest is the output check (a repetition skipped, merged or run out of order changes the dump), as it catches any wrong program. **What comes back with the loop, stated:** a solution may do work once in front of the repetitions (the point), and may get the repetitions wrong (counted as a wrong program; the read-out of any experiment on v6 names how many unusable programs changed the repetition loop or the `dummy` call); the agent's first region is the repetition loop again, as in E1-final. `dummy` is TSVC's name and in TSVC it does nothing; here it changes input values, and a model can read that in `main.c`. **Pass criteria, no model:** (1) output byte for byte v4's on the shipped and the perturbed input, every loop; (2) speed, one lane, variants interleaved (a scratch tool, `preflight/tools/speed_probe.py`): the expert reference in v6 — its temporary array obtained with malloc in front of the loop and released after it — within noise of v4's; beside it v5's reference as committed (the array kept in a `static` pointer) and v5's reference written the ordinary way (malloc and free in the function); (3) DiscoPoP's view of the loop under study as in v4, two draws on the server (`t0_17_server_a`, `t0_17_server_b`); (4) the order statement under prompt version 4 right on every profile, the repetition loop's own request included (`order_replay.py --repetition-loop`); (5) then the sizes (`t0_1_c2_sizes`), the classes in three draws (`t0_11_c2_a`, `t0_11_c2_b`, `t0_11_c2_c`) and the references through the harness (`t0_14_c2_refs`). **Also measured, because it was named as a cost of v5:** the data declared as arrays, as TSVC declares them, instead of pointers the compiler cannot tell apart (variant `c2arr`, prototype only); whole-program optimisation (`-flto`).
